feature: Expiry of queued Picco frontlight commands
implementation: A one-second monotonic deadline starts at request creation. The caller waits only for the remaining duration. The input worker rejects requests at or after the same deadline before invoking the driver.
assertions: No driver call at or after deadline
Live requests preserve brightness, warmth, success and driver errors
A caller that times out while the request remains queued cannot cause that expired request to invoke the driver later
commands: nix-shell --run 'cargo fmt --all && cargo test --locked -p femto-picco-board && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features desktop,femto-catalog/tailnet --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check'

firmware_manifest.installation_status: No automatic installer. Verify the actual device partition table and recovery backup before installation.

limits: Expiry does not cancel a driver operation already started; a caller timeout can still leave physical state unknown.
Host tests execute the actual firmware command module with an injected monotonic sample; physical I2C and scheduler behavior remain unqualified.
No full workspace test, native simulator, grayscale firmware or independent network rerun in this checkpoint.
